interactions.summary: After a student answers that Eve ate the fruit, Jiang makes the reversal explicit: Dante's Adam passage shifts responsibility for original sin from Eve to Adam, which Jiang calls revolutionary.

The class then explores why women are elevated in the Divine Comedy: one student says women are highly elevated as the spoken word, Jiang argues Beatrice teaches Dante and Mary outranks Jesus in heaven, and students propose responsibility-taking, identification of woman with love, and Adam's direct accountability to God.

claims.claim: Jiang reads Dante as relocating responsibility for original sin from Eve to Adam, and he treats that shift as revolutionary and heretical against conventional teaching.
He argues that the Divine Comedy persistently elevates women because Beatrice is Dante's teacher and Mary becomes the most elevated figure in heaven.
A student proposes that Dante may be telling readers to stop blaming women for everything and instead take ownership of their own acts.
Another student argues Adam bears primary responsibility because God warned him directly, whereas Eve received the warning only through Adam.

signature_moments.moment: The Eden story is flipped so that Adam, not Eve, becomes the accountable agent of the fall.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it's Adam and not Eve who was responsible
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's main reversal and a likely pressure point for the eventual public read and later lens work.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang intensifies the gender reversal by claiming heaven's highest instructional and devotional authority is feminine.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Mary is being elevated higher than Jesus
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Even if provocative, this is the lecture's sharpest way of marking Dante's challenge to ordinary hierarchy.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A student's shorthand for the elevated symbolic status women hold in the Divine Comedy.

uncertainty_notes.note: Several explanatory theories in this packet come from students rather than Jiang, so they should be treated as interpretive probes unless later packets explicitly endorse one.
